L121: (Redirected from 【54†All wheel drive】)
L122: The 【55†Jeep Wrangler】 (【56†TJ】 pictured) is a 【57†4×4】 four-wheel drive vehicle equipped with a low-range gearbox, which provides the driver with a selection between low range or high range gearing 【58†Hayes】 WHDX 70-170 【59†6×6】 tractor The 【60†8×8】 【61†tractor unit】 of the 【62†HETS】 (heavy equipment transport system)
L123: 
L124: An all-wheel drive^{【63†[1]】} vehicle (AWD^{【64†[2]】} vehicle) is one with a 【65†powertrain】 capable of providing power to all its wheels, whether full-time or on-demand.
L125: ## Types
L126: 
L127: [【66†edit】]
L128: 
L129: The most common forms of all-wheel drive are:
L130: 1x1
L131:     All 【67†unicycles】
L132: Reflects one axle with one wheel capable of being powered.
L133: 【68†2x2】
L134:     Some motorcycles and bikes
L135: Reflects two axles with one wheel on each capable of being powered.
L136: 4×4 (also, 【57†four-wheel drive】 or 4WD)
L137:     Reflects two axles with both wheels on each capable of being powered.
L138: 6×6 (also, 【69†six-wheel drive】 or 6WD)
L139:     Reflects three axles with both wheels on each capable of being powered.
L140: 【60†8×8】 (also, eight-wheel drive or 8WD)
L141:     Reflects four axles with both wheels on each capable of being powered.
L142: Vehicles may be either part-time all-wheel drive or full-time:
L143: 
L144: On-demand or Part-time
L145:     One axle is permanently connected to the drive, the other is connected as needed
L146: Full-time or Permanent
L147:     All axles are permanently connected, with or without a 【70†differential】.
L148: Independent
L149:     The wheels are driven, but not dependent on a central mechanical power coupling.
L150: ## Terminology
L151: 
L152: [【71†edit】]
L153: 
L154: In the context of 【72†hybrid】 and 【73†electric vehicles】, the North American designation of 'all-wheel-drive' may differ. In some hybrid vehicles, the combustion engine is only mechanically connected to the front wheels, while the rear wheels are powered independently by an electric motor; this may be marketed as eAWD. Furthermore, many electric vehicles have individual, unconnected motors powering each axle, or even each individual wheel, also without any center differential.
L155: ## Characteristics
L156: 
L157: [【74†edit】]
L158: 
L159: Further information: 【75†Four-wheel drive § SAE recommended practices】
L160: When tire grip is good during road driving, a 【70†differential】 is used between the axles to avoid 【76†driveline windup】. This is not required off-road, as the limited grip allows the tires to slip. All-wheel drive vehicles designed for extensive off-road use may not have such a differential, and so they suffer from wind-up when used on-road.^{【77†[3]】} Selectable 4WD also avoids this problem and requires only a simple 【78†dog clutch】 in the 【79†transfer case】, rather than a differential.
L161: For this reason, most early off-road vehicles used that system; e.g., 【80†Jeep】, 【81†Land Rover】.
L162: As vehicles became more sophisticated and tires gave better winter performance in the 1960s, there was an interest in giving the benefits of all-wheel drive to conventional cars: not for off-road use but for winter use in snow and ice or on wet roads. Exotic vehicles such as the high-powered 【82†Jensen FF】 followed by the 【83†AMC Eagle】, 【84†Subaru Leone】 and 【85†Audi Quattro】 series were the first to offer all-wheel drive in a high-speed road-based car.
L163: These, particularly the Quattro, would extensively develop this 【86†drivetrain】 with the use of 【87†viscous couplings】 and differentials to provide a safe and drivable car. The first off-road / on-road hybrids such as the 【88†Range Rover】 also chose the permanent all-wheel-drive system rather than manual selection.
